 The Honourable Smt. Justice M.G.Priyadarsini
 Civil Miscellaneous Appeal No.286 Of 2009
 And
 Cross Objections (Sr) No.36679 of 2009
Common Judgment

:
C.M.A.No.286 of 2009 is preferred by the Insurance Company, questioning the order and decree,
dated 22.01.2007 made in W.C.No.32 of 2006 on the file of the Commissioner for Workmen's Compensation and Assistant Commissioner of Labour, Nalgonda (for short, the learned Commissioner).
Challenging the very same order and decree, the claimant filed cross-objections No.36679 of 2009 seeking enhancement of compensation.
2. For the sake of convenience, hereinafter, the parties will be referred as per their array before the Commissioner.

3. The brief facts of the case are that the claimant has filed an application under the provisions of Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923 (amended as Employees' Compensation Act, 1923) claiming compensation of Rs.3,00,000/- alleging that he was employed by opposite party No.1 as driver on Auto bearing No. AP 24 V 7530, which was insured with opposite party No.2.

On 25.10.2005 while the claimant on the instructions of opposite party No.1 was driving MGP,J and CROSS OBJECTIONS (SR) No.36679 of 2009 the said auto from Modugula Mallepalli towards Marriguda along with passengers and at about 08:00 a.m., when he reached near the outskirts of P.K.Mallepalli, he lost control over the steering of the said Auto, due to which, the auto fell towards other side of the road.

sentences.text:
As a result, the claimant sustained fracture of right leg, fracture of right tibia,
fracture of right fibula, fracture of 2nd, 3rd and 4th ribs, grievous injuries on right side of chest and left hand.
Immediately, he was shifted to Government Hospital, Devarkonda and thereafter he took treatment privately.
He spent huge amounts towards his treatment.
Based on the complaint, the Police Station Chinthapalli of Nalgonda District registered a case in Crime No.130 of 2005 under Section 337 of IPC.

entities.text: Police Station Chinthapalli of Nalgonda District
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: According to the claimant, he was hale and healthy, aged 23 years, earning Rs.4,500/- per month as salary.
On account of fractures received by the claimant in the accident and on account of major operations, the claimant suffered permanent and unable to do any work.
The opposite party No.1 has terminated the claimant from services, thereby the claimant lost his total earning capacity from the date of accident.

Since, the auto was insured with opposite party No.2 and the insurance policy was subsisting as on the date of the accident, the opposite party No.1 being the employer and opposite party No.2 being the MGP,J and CROSS OBJECTIONS (SR) No.36679 of 2009 insurer of the said auto, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the claimant.

4. After receipt of notice, opposite party Nos.1 and 2 filed their respective written statements,
wherein the opposite party No.1 admitted the employment of the applicant as driver on a monthly M/S.The

On the other hand, the opposite party No.2 denied the employment of claimant under opposite party No.1.
It was further denied the manner of the accident, injuries sustained by the claimant, age and wages of the claimant.

It is also contended that the driver of the auto was not possessing valid and effective driving license to the drive the said auto and that the claim of the claimant is excessive and exorbitant and finally prayed to dismiss the application.
5. On behalf of the claimant, PWs.1 and 2 were examined and Exs.A1 to A7 were marked.
Exs.A1 to A3 are the certified copies of FIR, medical certificate and charge sheet.

Ex.A4 is the MGP,J and CROSS OBJECTIONS (SR) No.36679 of 2009 original disability certificate, Ex.A5 is the attested copy of driving licence of the claimant, Ex.A6 is the attested copy of R.C and Ex.A7 is the attested copy of Policy.

sentences.text: Whereas, on behalf of the opposite party No.2, none were examined, however, Ex.B1 copy of the insurance policy was marked.

6. The learned Commissioner after considering the evidence on record, both oral and documentary,
by determining the wages of claimant at Rs.3,214/- per month, loss of earning capacity as 40% and percentage of disability as 60% and by applying the factor '216.91' for the age of injured being 25 years, has awarded Rs.1,67,315/- towards compensation.

7. Dissatisfied by the impugned order, the claimant has filed Cross Objections No.36679 of 2009 for awarding interest @ 12% from the date of accident and whereas the insurance company has filed the Civil Miscellaneous Appeal to set aside the impugned order.

8. Heard learned Standing Counsel for the Insurance Company-opposite party No.2 and learned counsel for the claimant and perused the record.
9.

The main contention of the learned Standing Counsel for the Insurance Company is that though the claimant has not MGP,J and CROSS OBJECTIONS (SR) No.36679 of 2009 filed any documentary proof to show that has sustained the injuries, the PW.2, doctor-Orthopedic Surgeon,
has assessed the percentage of disability at 30% and loss of earning capacity at 50%, which is on higher side.

entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: He further contended that learned Commissioner has erroneously fixed the percentage of disability at 30% for the leg fracture which is completely healed and prayed to allow the appeal by setting aside the impugned order to the extent of opposite party No.2-Insurance Company.

10. It is further contention of the of the learned Standing Counsel for the Insurance Company is that in the absence of any cogent evidence to establish that there is employer- employee relationship between the claimant and the opposite party No. 1.
Whether there is employer-employee relationship between the claimant and opposite party No.1 is a question of fact and not a question of law.

sentences.text:
At the outset, we may take note of the fact, being a settled principle, that the question as to whether the employee met with an accident, whether the accident occurred during the course of employment, whether it arose out of an employment,
how and in what manner the accident occurred, who was negligent in causing the accident, whether there existed any relationship of employee and employer, what was the age and monthly salary of the employee, how many are the dependents of the deceased employee, the extent of disability caused to the employee due to injuries suffered in an accident, (2019) 11 SCC 514 MGP,J and CROSS OBJECTIONS (SR)
No.36679 of 2009 whether there was any insurance coverage obtained by the employer to cover the incident etc. are some of the material issues which arise for the just decision of the Commissioner in a claim petition when an employee suffers any bodily injury or dies during the course of his employment and he/his LRs sue(s) his employer to claim compensation under the Act.

10. The aforementioned questions are essentially the questions of fact and therefore,
they are required to be proved with the aid of evidence.
Once they are proved either way, the findings recorded thereon are regarded as the findings of fact.

11. The appeal provided under Section 30 of the Act to the High Court against the order of the Commissioner lies only against the specific orders set out in clauses (a)
to (e) of Section 30 of the Act with a further rider contained in the first proviso to the section that the appeal must involve substantial questions of law.

12. In other words, the appeal provided under Section 30 of the Act to the High Court against the order of the Commissioner is not like a regular first appeal akin to Section 96 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 which can be heard both on facts and law.

The appellate jurisdiction of the High Court to decide the appeal is confined only to examine the substantial questions of law arising in the case."
11.

In view of the principle laid down in the above said authority, it is clear that the above contention of the Insurance Company is not based on a question of law but it is purely a question of fact, which cannot be raised before this Court as per Section 30 of the Workmen's Compensation Act.
12.

On the other hand, learned counsel for the claimant contended that the claimant has proved his case by examining PW.2, Orthopedic Surgeon and also filed Ex.A4-Original Disability Certificate and Ex.A2-Medical Certificate, wherein, PW.2 has assessed the percentage of disability at 30% and loss of earning capacity at 50%.
However, the learned Commissioner MGP,J and CROSS OBJECTIONS (SR) No.36679 of 2009 erroneously restricted the percentage of earning capacity as 40%.

entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: He further contended that though the claimant stated that he was earning Rs.4,500/- per month under the employment of opposite party No.1, the learned commissioner fixed the monthly income of the claimant at Rs.3,214/-, which is very meager and needs to be enhanced.

He lastly contended that the learned Commissioner ought to have granted 12% interest per annum on the awarded compensation from the date of accident till the date of deposit as per the decision of Apex Court.

In view of the rival contentions, this Court perused the evidence available on record.

The claimant, who was examined as PW.1, has reiterated the contents of application in his evidence and filed Ex.A.1 certified copy of FIR; Ex.A.2 copy of medical certificate; Ex.A.3 copy of charge sheet;
Ex.A.4 original disability certificate; Ex.A.5 attested copy of driving licence of the claimant; Ex.A.6 attested copy of R.C. and Ex.A.7 attested copy of Policy.

The claimant also got examined PW.2,
Orthopedic Surgeon, who deposed that the claimant was suffering with post traumatic stiffness of both ankle and knee right.
He assessed the percentage of disability at 30% and loss of earning capacity at 50% as the claimant is not able to sit and squat to perform his earlier duties.
PWs.1 and 2 were cross- examined at length but nothing was elicited to discredit their MGP,J and CROSS OBJECTIONS (SR) No.36679 of 2009 evidence.

It is pertinent to state that except the self serving statement that the risk of the claimant being labourer was not covered by the insurance policy, the insurance company has neither adduced any evidence nor taken steps to prove the same.

Admittedly, the claimant met with an accident occurred on 25.10.2005 while he was discharging his duties as labourer under the employment of opposite party No. 1 as evident from Ex.A.1 and A.2,
FIR and Charge sheet, resulting in filing of the claim petition under the Workmen's Compensation Act seeking compensation of Rs.3,00,000/-.

The other contention of the learned counsel for the claimant was that the learned Commissioner erred in not awarding 12% interest from the date of accident till the date of deposit on the compensation amount.
As seen from the impugned order, the learned Commissioner has not awarded any interest on the compensation amount.
The finding of the learned Commissioner in not awarding interest on the compensation amount is not justifiable.

As per the Act and the decision of the Honourable Supreme Court in P. Meenaraj v. P.
Adigurusamy2, held as under:
"10.

As regards the date of commencement of the liability of interest, the learned counsel for the appellant appears to be right that even in the case of Pratap Narain Singh Deo (supra), this Court has not laid down the law 2 Civil Appeal No 209 of 2022, decided on 6 January 2022 MGP,J and CROSS OBJECTIONS (SR) No.36679 of 2009 that the interest would be payable only 30 days after the accident.

entities.text: MGP,J and CROSS OBJECTIONS (SR) No.36679 of 2009
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: In our view too, the said statutory period of 30 days does not put a moratorium over the liability of interest.
Such interest is related with the amount of compensation receivable by the claimant and there appears no reason for not allowing interest for 30 days from the date of accident.
In fact, in the referred decisions too, this Court has allowed interest from the date of accident.

That being the position, the questioned part of the order of the High Court calls for interference and the same is modified to the extent that the appellant would be entitled to interest from the date of accident."

14. In view of the principle laid down in the above said citation, it is evident that the claimant is entitled for interest at 12% per annum on the compensation amount from the date of accident till date of deposit.
Hence, this Court is inclined to award interest at 12% per annum on the compensation amount from the date of accident till the date of deposit.

15. Coming to the quantum of compensation, this Court is of the considered opinion that the learned Commissioner after considering the minimum wages fixed by the Government of Andhra Pradesh for the light vehicle driver employed in Public Motor Transport Undertakings and duly taking into M/S.The New India Assurance Co Ltd vs Sri Madyala Laxmaiah , Maddela Laxmaiah ... on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197793167/
4 consideration the age and avocation of the claimant, has rightly fixed the monthly income of the claimant at Rs.3,214/-, loss of earning capacity at 40%, applying relevant factor '216.91' as the claimant was aged about 25 years at time of accident, awarded MGP,J and CROSS OBJECTIONS (SR) No.36679 of 2009 the total compensation of Rs.1,67,315/- which is reasonable and needs no interference by this Court.
16.

sentences.text: Accordingly, while dismissing the Civil Miscellaneous Appeal No.286 of 2019 filed by the Insurance Company, the cross-objections filed by the claimant is partly allowed.

The order dated 22.01.2007 in W.C.No.32 of 2006 passed by the learned Commissioner for Workmen's Compensation and Assistant Commissioner of Labour at Nalgonda, is modified only to the extent of awarding interest at 12% per annum on the compensation awarded from the date of the accident till the date of deposit.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Pending Miscellaneous applications, if any, shall stand closed.
